tagline: Through the grasslands and down the old railroad grade to Nogales.
intro: ADOT's corridor plan starts the drive at I-10, where SR 83 runs south along the east side of the Santa Rita Mountains and tops out at about 5,085 feet in a pass between the Santa Ritas and the Empire Mountains. This was the road for the Empire Ranch, a 160-acre homestead in the 1870s that covered almost a million acres by 1906. At Sonoita SR 82 takes over and runs down the Sonoita Creek valley toward Nogales, in places on the very grade of the old railroad.
When Senator Jay Rockefeller drafted the national scenic byways law of 1991, his staff had toured this road and he borrowed from Arizona's statute.

moments.title: Sonoita
moments.text: The crossroads of the two highways, named from the O'odham for spring field. ADOT's plan calls the spring quarter horse show at its fairgrounds the oldest in the nation.

moments.title: Patagonia
moments.text: By the local museum's account, Welsh miners who knew the real Patagonia thought the mountains here looked like the Andes and named them accordingly. The old rail embankment along Sonoita Creek is a trail.

moments.title: Telles Grotto Shrine
moments.text: Near milepost 16, Juan and Juanita Telles built a shrine in thanks for their sons' safe return from the Second World War, and area residents have used it regularly.
